rationale:
Evidence: Iteration 7 raced the only design that reached 344.5. Its geometry was body_length 0.18, body_width 0.12, mass 0.8, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, and five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.05 m. Its controller was kp 2.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'search_left'. It finished 17 of 20 oval runs (mean progress 0.95, mean finish time 1.86 s). Iteration 8 changed only kd (0.25 to 0.4) and returned identical metrics to four decimals on all 60 trials, so kd in this range shows no measurable effect.

Correction to the draft: the draft's rationale treats the iteration-7 plant change (body_length 0.12, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.10, 8 mm sensors at y = 0.06) as verified. It was not. That geometry appeared only in a candidate that was never raced. The draft also dropped the two controller settings that produced the gain (ki 0.5 and line_loss 'search_left') and reverted to ki 0.1 and 'last_direction'. Its expected result therefore rests on an unverified plant and a controller that has not raced in the best configuration. I reject the draft.

What I kept: the verified iteration-7 design exactly, including its geometry, ki 0.5, line_loss 'search_left', base_speed 1.5 and kp 2.0. I set kd to 0.25, the raced value, since 0.25 and 0.4 gave identical results.

What I did not change: no new single-variable test. Iteration 8's kd test was neutral, and the line_loss test that could address the s-bend and slalom would risk the oval gain that is the only proven result. With two iterations left after this one, the safer use of this race is to confirm that the verified best reproduces its score, which also checks whether the simulator is reproducible for this design.

Expected result: score about 344.5, with oval completion near 0.85. The s-bend and slalom will still fail, with progress about 0.34 and 0.11. Success threshold: a score within about 1 point of 344.5. A deviation larger than that would indicate the race is not reproducible and would shift the next step toward robustness testing rather than new gains.
